state.sourced_data_flow: Meeting audio/video + email + phone -> transcription -> LLM extraction (summary, next steps, requirements, MEDDICC evidence) -> one-time entry -> fan-out to CRM custom fields, the room's notes, and the handoff packet.

repository_facts.MAP: WF-124 ships the Mutual Action Plan as a task graph. Its collections are wf124_plan, wf124_task, wf124_status_event and wf124_escalation in backend/dsr/mutual_action/plan.py.
repository_facts.domain_import_surface: backend/dsr/competitive_baseline/* may import only dsr.store. The enforced test test_wf122.py::test_the_domain_modules_import_nothing_but_the_store refuses any other dsr import, so a domain module cannot import dsr.mutual_action or dsr.crm.
repository_facts.shared_package: backend/dsr/competitive_baseline is owned by the merged WF-122 build. WF-135 adds one module file and edits none of its existing files.
repository_facts.no_crm_connection: This repository holds no live CRM connection. WF-038 models the CRM write as data (staged, submitted, updated, failed) and opens no socket.

alternatives.write_into_wf124: The fan-out also writes tasks into wf124_task. Cost: it writes a second feature's collection, so a WF-124 reshape breaks this workflow, and a capture would own rows another feature owns.
alternatives.three_owned_destinations: The fan-out writes only this feature's own collections and names the WF-124 plan id on the capture. Agreement is checked across the three destinations this build owns. Cost: agreement with the plan is a recorded reference, not a write.
alternatives.drop_the_map: Claim agreement across two destinations only. Cost: it drops a word from the sourced claim without recording what MAP means.

state.requirement: One entry reaches every destination, and a write that reaches one destination has not completed the workflow.

verdict.instructions: Given the sourced data flow, the repository facts and the three alternatives, should WF-135 fan out to the three destinations this feature owns and record the WF-124 plan id as a reference?

criteria.approve: Three owned destinations plus a recorded plan reference is the right shape: it keeps the fan-out inside one feature's collections and still traces the MAP claim.
criteria.revise: The shape is close but a named detail is wrong; the state says which.
criteria.reject: A different alternative is better; the state says which.

decision: WF-135: the capture writes one way, from the captured conversation out to the room's notes, the handoff packet and the CRM custom fields. No write back from the CRM into the local record is built.

state.sourced_vendor_phrase: Recapped: 'One-time data entry - Update information once and watch it populate everywhere through bi-directional CRM integrations'.
state.sourced_data_flow: one-time entry -> fan-out to CRM custom fields, the room's notes, and the handoff packet.

repository_facts.no_live_crm: This repository holds no live CRM connection. The CRM write is modelled as data with a state, and the outbound send is reported by the caller.
repository_facts.existing_crm_vocabulary: WF-038 names the per-row outcomes created, updated, submitted, failed, rejected and rolled_back in backend/dsr/crm_upsert/payloads.py. WF-135 reuses those names rather than inventing a second set.
repository_facts.domain_import_surface: The domain package may import only dsr.store, so the CRM vocabulary is re-declared with a note that names its source rather than imported.

alternatives.one_way_out: Write from the capture to the three destinations. A CRM change reaches the local record only when a later capture carries it. Cost: a field edited in the CRM does not appear here until the next conversation.
alternatives.bi_directional: Also poll or receive the CRM's field changes and write them back onto the capture. Cost: this repository has no CRM subscription, no webhook receiver for this workflow and no conflict rule for the same field written twice, so the reverse half would be unverifiable.

state.requirement: The build must not claim a capability it cannot verify.

verdict.instructions: The vendor phrase promises bi-directional sync, but the data flow describes only a fan-out and this repository has no live CRM connection. Should WF-135 build the one-way write and record the reverse half as not built?

criteria.approve: One-way write is the honest build: it delivers the sourced fan-out and records the reverse half as not built.
criteria.revise: The decision is close but a named detail is wrong; the state says which.
criteria.reject: The reverse half should be built anyway; the state says which.

decision: WF-135: transcription and extraction arrive through this feature's API as data. The build makes no call to Whisper, no call to an LLM and no call to a CRM. MEDDICC evidence is captured per letter with a coverage report and no score, because the research names MEDDICC evidence as an output of the extraction and records that no open-source product enforces MEDDICC.

state.workflow: Auto-capture of the deal conversation into the CRM
state.sourced_extensibility: Open-source: this is a glue problem with no single OSS answer - self-hosted Whisper for transcription, an LLM for extraction, n8n / Windmill / Kestra for orchestration, RudderStack for the CDP write, and Nextcloud/Docmost for the store. There is no OSS MEDDICC-enforcing conversation-intelligence product of note.
state.sourced_outputs: The extraction yields summary, next steps, requirements and MEDDICC evidence. Four outputs, not one.

repository_facts.domain_import_surface: The enforced test test_wf122.py::test_the_domain_modules_import_nothing_but_the_store allows only dsr.store inside backend/dsr/competitive_baseline, so the module stays importable with no network.
repository_facts.no_network_in_tests: The backend suite runs with no network, so a module that called a transcription or an LLM endpoint could not be tested.
repository_facts.existing_crm_vocabulary: WF-038 records a CRM write as data with the outcomes created, updated, submitted, failed, rejected and rolled_back. This build stores the CRM field payload and records its state.

alternatives.extraction_is_data: The caller (the recorder, or an n8n/Kestra job) posts the transcript and the extraction result. This build validates, stores, fans out and reports agreement. Cost: the caller must supply the four outputs.
alternatives.call_the_llm_here: The feature calls an LLM itself. Cost: a key, a network call and a test that cannot run offline, for a vendor-neutral pipeline the research does not fix.
alternatives.score_meddicc: Score each letter and gate on a total. Cost: the research names no scale and no product that enforces one, so the number would be invented and would read as a standard.

state.requirement: The domain module must stay importable and testable with no network, and the build must not imply a vendor parity it does not have.

contract_compliance.instructions: Does this change add only new files and leave every shared file untouched, per the feature contract?

criteria.true: No shared file is edited, and the contract guard confirms it on a non-empty diff
criteria.false: A shared file is edited, or the guard did not actually measure a diff

claims_backed_by_measurement.instructions: Is every claim made in the evidence supported by a measurement that was actually run, rather than asserted, read off a progress bar, or produced by a check that passed on empty input? Declared limits are not a failure of this question -- they are the honest disclosure that belongs to them.

criteria.true: Each claim traces to quoted, reproducible tool output
criteria.false: A claim is asserted, or a check passed vacuously or was not run

coverage_of_the_change.instructions: Setting aside what is declared unverified, how much of the change did the evidence actually exercise? Judge breadth, not honesty: a declared limit is fine, but a large unexamined surface is not.

criteria.true: Every surface the change introduces is exercised by a measurement, with at most incidental limits declared
criteria.false: A substantial part of the change was never measured, whether or not that is declared

audit_integrity.instructions: Does this change preserve the audited-store guarantee: all writes through the wrapper, no direct database connection, no schema change outside the envelope?

criteria.true: Writes go through the audited store and the envelope is unchanged
criteria.false: A direct connection is opened, or a typed column or migration is added

design_floor.instructions: Does the frontend meet the design floor -- 44px touch targets, visible focus, a text label beside every icon, no emoji as icons, reduced motion respected -- as checked by the scripted pass?

criteria.true: The scripted design-floor pass is green
criteria.false: The pass is red, was skipped, or is on the allowlist

verdict.instructions: Should this change land on main? Weigh the balance of the questions above rather than deciding on your own: where contract_compliance, audit_integrity and design_floor are all healthy and the evidence questions show broad coverage, answer merge with the confidence that warrants. Items listed as unverified are declared context to weigh, not defects in themselves -- but a change whose coverage is genuinely thin, or which was recovered from a base far behind main and not reconciled, is fix.
